diagnosis.H3: Using real island covariates plus distance/climate-dependent visitor assembly reproduces the corrected isolation-to-pollen-limitation slope closely.
diagnosis.H2_selfing: Isolation-driven assurance response is broadly recoverable; three of four context coefficients are within two empirical SE in the best draw and northern mid-latitude is just outside.
diagnosis.H2_generalization: Contemporary adaptive response to visitor assembly does not reproduce the corrected positive generalized-accessible|selfing slopes. Best-draw coefficients are negative in all four contexts.
diagnosis.H4_assurance: The sign remains opposite to the empirical exact-species association. Within-island lineages experiencing poor current pollination evolve higher assurance, creating compensatory positive trait-PL covariance that overwhelms assurance's direct reduction of pollen limitation.
diagnosis.structural_inference: The remaining mismatch is consistent with a missing colonization/assembly filter. Chapter 1 measures composition of island floras, where high-assurance and accessible species can be preferentially admitted under isolation before or in addition to within-island adaptation.

claim_boundary: Model3R-v2 is a prospective negative result; no larger search of the same structure is authorized as a rescue.
H3 reproduction alone does not constitute realistic reproduction of the Chapter 1 island syndrome.
H1 atomic and colour holdouts remained unused.
The v2 failure motivates an assembly/colonization filter because that process is directly relevant to the contemporary island-flora composition analysed in Chapter 1.
